items.title: [Question][ROCm] GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer: does the 640-token block table reach 32-pool pages on gfx942/gfx950 too?
items.bodyExcerpt:
We found this on hardware vLLM doesn't support (gfx1030, Radeon Pro V620), running GLM-5.3-Flash without aiter. The code path involved is shared with gfx942/gfx950, and we have no MI300/MI355 to check it on. Could someone with one confirm or rule it out?

**What we see.** `Glm5NextIndexerCache` stores pooled keys in pages of 32 pools (storage block 128 tokens at `index_kpool=4`). The hybrid KDA page rule makes the attention block 640. On ROCm the sparse-MLA and indexer backends accept `MultipleOf(16)` (`get_supported_kernel_block_sizes`), so `select_common_block_size` keeps kernel block 640. The indexer metadata builder only converts the table when the storage block is a multiple of the kernel block (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`, prefill and decode branches; unchanged on main):

```python
if (
    kernel_block_size is not None
    and self.kv_cache_spec.block_size != kernel_block_size
    and self.kv_cache_spec.block_size % kernel_block_size == 0
):
    factor = self.kv_cache_spec.block_size // kernel_block_size
    indexer_block_table = (block_table[:, ::factor] // factor).contiguous()
```

128 % 640 ≠ 0, so the 640-token table goes to `get_compressed_slot_mapping` (the kpool writer) and to `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache_triton` as if each entry named one 32-pool page. With per-chunk block allocation:
- pools written before their block exists land in padding;
- positions past the allocated blocks alias block 0;
- positions past the 52-column table (at `max_model_len` 32768) are masked by the gather.

On NVIDIA the kernel block is 64, so the `// factor` branch applies. As far as we can tell nothing here is aiter-specific: the kpool path uses `forward_cuda` on ROCm whether aiter is on or off.

**Reproducer.** One GPU, stock vLLM only, no model: [`repro_rocm_kpool_table.py`](https://github.com/Omnicef/vllm/blob/glm53-v030/tests/local/repro_rocm_kpool_table.py). It writes a 9,432-token prompt in the served prefill chunks with the real ROCm kpool writer

items.title: [Bug]: RecoverSSM align mode commits the final SSM state to an unwritten block at exact block boundaries (floor vs ceil-1)
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

Reproduced on a downstream fork, not on stock vLLM: Morrowmake/vllm-cmp170hx 1.7.0 (`v0.30.1rc1.dev368+gc1ce6491e`). It routes GLM-5 KDA layers through the Kimi-K3 RecoverSSM kernels. 4× SM80 GPUs (CMP 170HX, 64 GB), TP4, DFlash spec decode, prefix caching on (`mamba_cache_mode=align`), Mamba block size 1152.

Both affected lines are unchanged on `main` @ 0872ddf4b96d.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

In align mode, RecoverSSM puts the final committed state in column `floor(x / B)`. The rest of the align path uses `ceil(x / B) - 1`:

- `vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py:1482`: `prev_state_idx = (num_computed_tokens - 1) // block_size`
- `vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py:467`: `dest_block_idx = aligned_new_computed // block_size - 1`

The two RecoverSSM sites:

- `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/recoverssm.py:287` (`_prepare_commit_plan_kernel`): `final_num_computed // mamba_block_size`
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/recoverssm.py:97` (`_postprocess_recoverssm_align_kernel`): `(num_computed + num_sampled) // MAMBA_BLOCK_SIZE`

The two conventions agree except when `x` is an exact multiple of `B`. There they differ, and that happens when a verify step ends exactly on a block boundary with all drafts accepted. RecoverSSM then commits the state to column `k`, while the next step reads its recurrent and conv state from a block this request never wrote. New Mamba blocks are not zeroed (#56524), so the state is garbage, or another request's state.

Observed effect: generation loses context mid-word a few tokens after a multiple of 1152, then repeats a token until `max_tokens` (`…Inputhandlehandlehandle…`, `locklocklock…`).

Found and diagnosed by @YulHeon in Morrowmake/glm53-flash-cmp170hx-recipe#7, which has the boundary-position analysis.

**Proposed fix**: use `ceil - 1` in both places. It does not change anything when `x` is not a multiple of `B`.

items.title: [Bugfix] Forward upstream error message in Anthropic streaming converter (#46028)
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #46028.

When the engine fails mid-stream, the OpenAI serving layer emits an `ErrorResponse` payload (`{"error": {...}}`) via `create_streaming_error_response`, followed by `[DONE]`. The Anthropic adapter's `message_stream_converter` validated **every** chunk as a `ChatCompletionStreamResponse`, so the error chunk raised a pydantic `ValidationError`. The outer `except` then re-emitted that as a generic `internal_error` carrying the *pydantic* message — masking the real upstream failure. The reporter hit this serving GLM-5.2, where an engine 500 surfaced only as `2 validation errors for ChatCompletionStreamResponse ... model Field required input_value={'error': {'message': 'Internal Server Error'...}}`.

This PR detects the error payload (new `parse_streaming_error_chunk` helper, mirroring the existing module-level `wrap_data_with_event` helper) and forwards its message as an Anthropic `error` event, reusing the converter's existing `AnthropicStreamEvent(type="error", ...)` shape. Only the failure path changes; valid chunks validate exactly as before.

## Not a duplicate

- `gh pr list --search "46028 in:body"` → none.
- `gh pr list --search "message_stream_converter"` → only #45807 (stop_sequence `stop_reason`), unrelated.
- #34053 (`[Anthropic API]` 6 protocol bugs) also edits `serving.py`, but for message/tool-call ID and `tool_result` formats; it does not touch the streaming error path.

## Test Plan / Test Result

Added CPU-only unit test `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_stream_error.py` (the existing `test_messages.py` needs a live server):

items.title: [Bugfix] Pick a KV block size supported by every attention backend
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #48286.

`Platform.update_block_size_for_backend()` picks the KV cache block size from the **first** non-SSM attention backend only. Models that mix attention backends with disjoint block-size support break: GLM-DSA / DeepSeek-V3.2-style models pair a sparse-MLA main backend (`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, supports `[32, 64]`, prefers 32) with `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend` (supports only `[64]`). The auto-selected 32 then fails much later in `select_common_block_size()` with the opaque

```
ValueError: No common block size for 32.
```

and the only workaround is a manual `--block-size 64` (undocumented, as #48286 notes).

This PR was split in two to keep the diff reviewable. It now carries backend collection and block-size selection only (+131/-21). Aligning phases 2 and 3 to the full backend list follows in a separate PR once this one merges.

## Changes

- `Platform._find_non_ssm_backend()` becomes `_find_non_ssm_backends()` and returns every distinct non-SSM backend in layer order rather than the first. Both call sites are updated (`interface.py`, `cpu.py`); no caller of the old name remains.
- New `Platform._preferred_block_size_for_backends()` returns the smallest block size every backend accepts:
  - a single backend keeps today's behaviour via `get_preferred_block_size()`;
  - if every backend accepts the default, the default wins;
  - otherwise candidates are the least common multiples formed by taking one supported size per backend, tried in ascending order, and **each candidate is confirmed against every backend** via `supports_block_size()`;
  - if nothing is common it raises `ValueError` naming each backend and its supported sizes.
- Candidates are validated rather than inferred. A backend may override `supports_block_size()` to accept exact sizes only, as CPU_MLA does by accepting 16 but no multiple of it, so "a multiple of a supported size" is not a safe assumption. items.title: [Bugfix][KV Offloading] Fix CPU offload block count mismatch across PP ranks
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation

Native CPU offloading computes CPU cache capacity from each worker's KV cache tensors. Under pipeline parallelism, workers may own different numbers or types of layers, so different PP ranks can derive different CPU offload block counts.

The scheduler uses the first worker's KV cache config, while workers build offloading specs from their local configs. If the scheduler-side CPU block count is larger than a worker's local CPU buffer capacity, offloaded block IDs can exceed that worker's allocated CPU cache range.

### Runtime Validation

  I reproduced the issue with vLLM v0.26.0 using:

  - Model: `GLM-5.2-NVFP4`
  - `pipeline_parallel_size=4`
  - `tensor_parallel_size=1`
  - Native CPU offloading via `OffloadingConnector`
  - Prefix caching enabled
  - No SSD offloading

  Before the fix, different PP ranks computed different CPU offload block counts from their local KV cache tensors:

  ```text
  scheduler/rank0 CPU num_blocks: 35341
  worker/rank0 CPU num_blocks: 35341
  worker/rank1 CPU num_blocks: 34435
  worker/rank2 CPU num_blocks: 34435
  worker/rank3 CPU num_blocks: 36561
  ```
  This confirms the mismatch. Since the scheduler allocates CPU block IDs based on its own CPU block count, rank1/rank2 only had capacity for 34435 blocks while the scheduler could allocate IDs up to 35340. Those IDs would be outside rank1/rank2's CPU buffer range.

  After applying the fix, all PP ranks used the same unified minimum CPU block count:
  ```text
  scheduler CPU num_blocks: 34435
  worker/rank0 CPU num_blocks: 34435
  worker/rank1 CPU num_blocks: 34435
  worker/rank2 CPU num_blocks: 34435
  worker/rank3 CPU num_blocks: 34435
  ```
  The fixed server also started successfully and returned successful responses:

  GET /health -> 200
  POST /v1/completions -> 200

  ### Proposed Changes

  - Add `num_cpu_blocks` to `KVCacheConfig` and `OffloadingConfig`.
  - Compute CPU offload block capacity for every worker KV

## Purpose

Two related changes, both following the review on this PR:

1. **Fix a soundness bug in `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_decode_logprobs_match_prefill_logprobs`.** The test rebuilt each prefill prefix from *text* and re-encoded it; `encode(decode(ids))` is not lossless for BPE tokenizers, so the "prefill" could evaluate a different token sequence than decode did and report false mismatches. The prefix is now built directly from token ids (`prompt_token_ids + decode_token_ids[:i]`), which also removes an O(N²) extra `llm.generate` per decoded token. This is the fix from #43317 (@Evangade), carried here at the maintainer's request after that PR went stale; the standalone tokenizer regression test from #43317 is dropped per the review there. Original report by @xRay2016 in #27433.
2. **Add `zai-org/glm-4-9b-chat` and `microsoft/phi-4` to the tested-model list**, following the [invitation to submit model validations without a separate issue](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53247#issuecomment-5374419058).

Why the fix matters here: GLM was originally removed from this PR because the official suite reported a decode/prefill mismatch. items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Honor modality-scoped mm_processor_kwargs in every model that reads them
items.bodyExcerpt:
> **Update 2026-10-03:** `get_image_size_with_most_features` is now sized per modality (image by default, video for video tokens). See "The size bound follows the modality being sized" below.

> **Update 2026-09-30:** #56372 removed `get_merged_mm_kwargs(..., modality=)`, which the text below describes. The reads now go through `InputProcessingContext.get_modality_mm_kwargs(kwargs, modality)`: the resolved kwargs, with that modality's scope overlaid for vLLM-side reads. Each call site's change is otherwise unchanged. `mistral3` and `qwen2_5_omni_thinker` now match `main` (#56372 fixed mistral3 itself). Details and a fresh test run: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54527#issuecomment-5905006141

Follow-up to #53808.

## Background

#53808 taught `get_merged_mm_kwargs` to overlay HF-style nested
`images_kwargs` / `videos_kwargs` / `audio_kwargs` onto the flat namespace, and
threaded a `modality` argument through Qwen2-VL and Qwen3-VL. Its docstring
states the rule:

> When `modality` is set, HF-style nested `images_kwargs` / `videos_kwargs` /
> `audio_kwargs` are overlaid onto the flat namespace for vLLM-side reads
> (token budgets, dummy inputs). Processor construction and HF `__call__`
> should omit `modality` so the nested dicts still reach the HF processor.

Every model outside the Qwen family that predicts sizes or token counts from
those kwargs was left reading the flat namespace only. The HF processor honors
the nested dict in its `__call__`, so vLLM and the processor disagree about how

items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Cap the DynamicVideoBackend sampling fps
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`DynamicVideoBackend` (`vllm/multimodal/video.py`, registered as `opencv_dynamic`)
sizes its frame-candidate walk directly from the request-supplied `fps`, so the
amount of work is unbounded by anything in the video:

```python
fps = target.fps
...
if duration <= max_duration:
    n = int(math.floor(duration * fps))
    frame_indices_list = sorted(
        {min(max_frame_idx, math.ceil(i / fps * original_fps)) for i in range(n)}
    )
```

`n` scales with `fps`, but the *result* does not: the largest index reachable is
`duration * original_fps` regardless, and the set deduplicates at the end. So a
large `fps` buys nothing and costs CPU linearly.

This applies the same clamp the sibling backends in this file already use —
`_MAX_FPS: ClassVar[int] = 30` plus `fps = min(target.fps, cls._MAX_FPS)`, which
is verbatim what `QwenVLVideoBackend` (`:362`/`:373`, from the merged #56729) and
`GLMGAVideoBackend` (`:812`/`:839`) do.

## Reachability

`fps` is request-controlled through `media_io_kwargs`, and nothing strips it for
this backend:

1. `opencv_dynamic` is registered with `video_processor="Glm4vVideoProcessor"`,
   so it is the **default** backend on GLM-4V-family servers — a plain
   `POST /v1/chat/completions` with
   `"media_io_kwargs": {"video": {"fps": 100000}}` is enough, no override needed.
2. It registers with the default `requires_gpu=False`, so
   `VideoMediaIO.merge_kwargs` (`vllm/multimodal/media/video.py:60`) does **not**
   strip a request-level `video_backend: "opencv_dynamic"` either. The remaining
   `merge_kwargs` handling forwards `fps` verbatim.
3. It is also selected explicitly at
   `vllm/model_executor/models/nano_nemotron_vl.py:830`.

Only the `duration <= max_duration` branch is exposed. The `else` branch
self-bounds: `num_samples >= total_frames_num` short-circuits, and otherwise
`num_samples < total_frames_num`.

## Measured cost

Measured on a verbatim extraction of the function body (pure Python/numpy, so

items.title: [Perf] JIT monitor: hook TileLang JITImpl.compile instead of __call__
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

The JIT monitor is switched on after warmup, and it wraps TileLang's `JITImpl.__call__`. As a result, every TileLang kernel launch pays for the wrapper, including building the cache-miss key, even though nearly all of those calls hit the kernel cache. TileLang's `__call__` only calls `self.compile()` on a cache miss, so this PR hooks `compile` instead. The monitor still catches every post-warmup JIT compile, and cache hits no longer go through it.

This matters for models with many TileLang launches outside CUDA graphs. For example, GLM-5.3-Flash runs ~72 mhc TileLang calls per eager step (prefill / mixed batches).

**Not a duplicate:** I searched open PRs for jit_monitor / TileLang and found nothing related.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/jit_monitor/` (the fake `JITImpl` now calls `compile()` on a cache miss, like the real one).
- Microbench: 2000 `mhc_post_tilelang` calls after warmup, with the monitor off and on, on H100.
- E2E: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, TP8 on H100, fp8 KV, MTP with 5 speculative tokens, async scheduling. Benchmark: `vllm bench serve` with random 1024 in / 128 out, each point run twice.

## Test Result

Unit tests: 25 passed, 7 skipped.

Microbench (µs per call):

| | monitor off | monitor on |
|---|---|---|
| main (wrap `__call__`) | 15.7 | 25.9 |
| this PR (wrap `compile`) | 15.5 | 15.6 |

That's ~10 µs × ~72 calls ≈ 0.7 ms of CPU per eager step removed on GLM-5.3-Flash.

E2E, mean TTFT / median TTFT / mean TPOT (ms), average of 2 runs:

| | c=1 | c=8 | c=32 |
|---|---|---|---|

## Purpose

Fixes #58315. Related to #58105.

Under `tool_choice="required"` (and named tool choice) vLLM constrains generation
with an xgrammar structural tag built from xgrammar's builtin model templates.
Those templates spell the tool-call markers as **strings**
(`TriggeredTagsFormat(triggers=["<tool_call>"])`, `TagFormat(begin="<tool_call>get_weather", end="</tool_call>")`),
so the grammar admits any tokenization of that text, including `<` `tool_call` `>`
assembled from ordinary sub-tokens.

The streaming parser engine, once it has seen token IDs, recognises the markers listed
in `token_id_terminals` only by their dedicated token ID
(`StreamingParserEngine._process_lex_tokens`, `strict` branch) and treats the assembled
spelling as content. The two sides therefore disagree on what a tool call is:

| encoding of `<tool_call>get_current_time</tool_call>` (GLM-5) | grammar | parser |
|---|---|---|
| dedicated ids `[154843, ..., 154844]` | accept | 1 tool call |
| ordinary ids `[27, 14163, 13420, 29, ..., 522, 14163, 13420, 29]` | **accept** | **0 tool calls, text in `content`** |

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash cannot run with decode context parallelism. Its kpool sparse indexer compresses the indexer KV (`index_kpool=4`), and the indexer metadata builder rejects DCP whenever `compress_ratio > 1`. This check does not depend on the platform or the attention backend:

```
NotImplementedError: DCP is not supported with sparse indexer KV compression (compress_ratio=4)
```

This PR shards the kpool indexer across DCP ranks by pool:

- `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size` must be a multiple of `index_kpool` (e.g. 4), so each compressed pool lives entirely on one rank. The builder now raises a clear error when this does not hold.
- `CompressedSlotMappingKernel` is DCP-aware. Each rank writes only the compressed states it owns, at rank-local positions. Prefill chunk metadata uses the interleave measured in compressed units.

## Purpose

This supersedes #55543 by @Leoyzen, who is kept as co-author. It enables the `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache on SM90 for rope-free sparse-MLA models with head_size 512, such as GLM-5.3-Flash, through `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`.

items.title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Pass per-sequence context lengths to the AITER paged MQA-logits kernels
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Error

MTP with native DSA-indexer decode above `next_n=2` crashes during warm-up on MI355X (seen at `next_n=3` and `next_n=6`). GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4, `num_speculative_tokens=5` (`next_n=6`), Gluon paged MQA logits:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-4 (Agent handle: 0x20465ea0) on address 0x792dc0bf1000. Reason: Unknown.
```

Where it does not crash, the indexer silently uses wrong causal bounds: in a direct call at `next_n=3`, the 8192-token sequence loses its last 2 valid positions in every row (9/12 rows correct).

## Cause

With native decode (`next_n > 1`), `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` receives a `(B, next_n)` table of per-row context lengths, `[b, j] = L_b - next_n + j + 1`, built in [`indexer.py#L1136-L1152`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2df122e65e87dc12870ce5f0180b49f012e7a53b/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py#L1136-L1152). The AITER Gluon `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` and `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1` kernels read the table as a flat `[B]` array and some sequences get another row's length.

Example: 4 requests, `next_n=3`, context lengths 8192 / 1500 / 3000 / 700:

| `b` | `j=0` | `j=1` | `j=2` | `L_b` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 8190 | 8191 | **8192** | 8192 |
| 1 | 1498 | 1499 | **1500** | 1500 |
| 2 | 2998 | 2999 | **3000** | 3000 |
| 3 | 698 | 699 | **700** | 700 |

The kernel expects `[8192, 1500, 3000, 700]` and computes each row's bound itself. Reading the `(4, 3)` table as `[4]`, it gets the first four values in memory, `[8190, 8191, 8192, 1498]`: request 0 loses its last 2 positions in every row, and requests 1 to 3 get lengths past their own KV pages, the likely source of the fault. Column `j = next_n - 1` equals `L_b`, which is what the kernel needs.

## Fix

Pass the kernels the last column, which is the per-sequence length. `[B]` and `(B, 1)` inputs, the C4A Triton path and the torch fallback are unchanged.

items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Retire stale Mamba spec blocks in prefill checkpoint steps
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

With MTP and prefix caching on, hybrid models such as GLM-5.3-Flash can return garbage when a request reuses a cached prompt prefix. Some prefill steps save a checkpoint of the linear-attention state in the middle of a chunk. In those steps the scheduler leaves an unused MTP scratch block in the slot that belongs to the checkpoint. That block is never written, yet it is registered in the prefix cache ahead of the real checkpoint, so later requests resume from it. This change moves the scratch block out of the way in those steps too, as already happens in every other step.

The skip was added together with internal checkpoints in #53614. GLM-5.3-Flash reaches this path since #56960. The branch is based on current main (58b3298457). No open PR changes speculative-block relocation; #57128 changes the Mamba lookup and does not touch this path.

## Claims

- Fixes persistent garbage output after prefix-cache hits for hybrid models with internal prefill checkpoints and MTP, for example GLM-5.3-Flash with `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`.
- No behavior change without speculative decoding, for `mamba_cache_mode` other than `align`, or for steps without an internal checkpoint.

## Validation

Setup: RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 on 2 H200 GPUs, served with default settings plus MTP:

```
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}'
```

Reproducer (script below): send a long prompt while another long prompt is still being processed, then send the exact same prompt again. The second request reuses the cached start of the prompt.

- Before the fix, the second answer was garbage in 3 of 3 trials, for example `File: /home/erdos/2024/4/4  # File: /home/erdos/2024/4/4 ...`, while the first answer was a normal list of function names.
- With the fix, both answers were normal in 3 of 3 trials.

## Summary

This PR routes the GLM-5.2 (GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM) fused QKV-A projection
through the existing `min_latency_fused_qkv_a_proj` custom op backed by
`dsv3_fused_a_gemm`, eliminating the cuBLASLt split-K + splitKreduce kernel pair
at decode batch size 1. The `dsv3_fused_a_gemm` C++ kernel already supports the
GLM-5.2 fused-QKV-A shape with a warp-specialized fused-A kernel that folds the
split-K reduction inside the CTA -- the same kernel SGLang uses for this projection.
The custom op has a registered `fake_impl`, making it torch.compile-safe and CUDA-graph
capture-safe.

The core change widens `_can_use_min_latency_fused_qkv_a_gemm` to accept the
GLM-5.2 fused-QKV-A weight shape alongside the existing DeepSeek-V3 shape. This
collapses two kernel launches per layer (splitK GEMM + splitKreduce) into a single

SM90+ for additional latency reduction at low token counts.

Because the fused-QKV-A custom-op path is frozen into the CUDA graph at capture time,

items.title: [Bugfix][DCP] Sort DCP group ranks so rank_in_group matches collective order
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Fix garbage output when a DCP group spans TP × PCP (e.g. TP2 × PCP2 × DCP4): sort each DCP group's ranks so `rank_in_group` agrees with the order collectives return shards in.

## Claims

- TP2 × PCP2 × DCP4 on GLM-5.3-NVFP4 goes from GSM8K 0.000 to 0.905.
- No change for DCP groups that were already ascending (DCP within TP, or DCP == PCP), which covers every previously validated configuration.

## Validation

GSM8K (5-shot) on 4x B300, MRV2, GLM-5.3-NVFP4, `-tp 2 -pcp 2 -dcp 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla -cc.cudagraph_mode=NONE`:

| | GSM8K |
|---|---:|
| main | 0.000 |
| this PR | 0.905 |

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_dcp_a2a.py -k test_dcp_group_ranks_match_collective_order  # 5 passed
```

## Details

**Root cause.** With PCP, `initialize_model_parallel` builds a DCP group that spans TP × PCP PCP-first (`all_ranks.transpose(-1, -2)`), giving member lists like `[0, 2, 1, 3]`.
- `torch.distributed.new_group` sorts its ranks, so all-gathers return shards in global-rank order.
- `GroupCoordinator.rank_in_group` is `ranks.index(rank)` on the unsorted list.
- The DCP LSE merge (`correct_attn_out`) uses `rank_in_group` to pick this rank's LSE from the gathered LSEs. So DCP ranks 1 and 2 rescaled their partial outputs with each other's LSE.

This was found by comparing each rank's attention partials against a torch reference and merging them offline: every rank's partials were correct and only the merge was wrong. The new unit test checks that DCP groups are ascending for TP-only, PCP-only and TP × PCP layouts.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR touches DCP group rank order (searched "dcp rank order", "DCP group ranks").

items.title: [Bugfix][DSv3.2] Carry the shared indexer top-k across pipeline stages
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Fix a GSM8K accuracy loss on GLM-5.x / DeepSeek-V3.2-style models under pipeline parallelism. These models reuse the previous layer's indexer top-k, and when a PP stage starts on a reusing layer, that stage read a stale top-k. This PR sends the top-k along with the intermediate tensors.

## Claims

- GLM-5.3-NVFP4 PP2 × TP2 on main: GSM8K 0.879 → 0.908. Before the fix, stage 1's first three layers attend with the previous step's top-k.
- With gather-based DCP (#59916), where it was more visible: 0.820 → 0.908.
- Only stage boundaries that land on a top-k-reusing layer send anything extra (`(num_tokens, index_topk)` int32 per step). Other models and partitions are unchanged.

## Validation

GSM8K (5-shot, all 1319 q) on 4x B300, MRV2, GLM-5.3-NVFP4, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla -cc.cudagraph_mode=NONE`:

| config | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| `-pp 2 -tp 2` | 0.879 | 0.908 |
| `-pp 2 -tp 2 -dcp 2` with gather DCP (#59916) | 0.820 | 0.908 |
| same, `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=38,40` (boundary aligned to a top-k group), no fix | 0.882 | - |

## Details

**Root cause.** GLM-5.3 sets `index_topk_freq=4` with offset 3, so groups of layers reuse the top-k computed by the group's first layer.
- The default PP2 split puts the stage boundary at layer 39, which is inside a group.
- Stage 1's first layers (39-41) therefore skip the indexer and read `topk_indices_buffer`. On that stage the buffer holds the top-k of the previous step's last indexer layer, for the previous batch.
- Aligning the partition (38/40) restored accuracy, which confirms the cause.

**Fix.** `reuses_previous_topk(config, layer_id)` is factored out of the attention init.
- The model adds `topk_indices` to its intermediate tensors when any stage starts on a reusing layer.
- The receiving stage copies it into its top-k buffer.

Only the NVIDIA `deepseek_v32` model path is patched. The AMD path has the same structure and could get the same fix in a follow-up.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8x MI355X at 1M context gets about 32 GiB more KV cache per GPU.
- The CUDA path and shared worker / model-runner code are unchanged.

## Validation

End-to-end on 8x MI355X (gfx950) with dummy weights:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --load-format dummy -tp 8 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}'
```

|---|---|---|
| main (`89439db727`) | 174.95 GiB | 90,340,997 tokens |
| this PR | 206.92 GiB | 106,889,551 tokens |

The 31.97 GiB difference matches the expected saving: (8192 − 96) rows × 1M columns × 4 B ≈ 31.6 GiB. With the fix, 16 concurrent completions (prompts of 301–4801 tokens, 32 output tokens each) all finished with no workspace errors. That confirms the smaller locked workspace still covers real decode steps.

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] gfx950 device length aware top-k split policy for k=2048
items.bodyExcerpt:
This fixes #55327.

The change generalizes `topKPerRowDecodeGfx950DeviceLengthAware` to work with different values of k, and adds `gfx950TopK2048ActiveBlocks`. The grid still only depends on `numRows`, so graph capture stays stable, and the number of splits is now determined on device per row, ensuring that there are at least 2048 real indices in each split. Rows under 4096 can be processed by a single block, skipping the merge step.

GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 use `index_topk` 2048, which goes through the generic path on gfx950 and has 10 splits. In the merge step, all 20480 candidates are processed by a single block for each row. For rows with fewer active tokens this can lead to significant overhead. With this PR, the number of candidates per row in the merge step will be reduced to between 0 and 12288, a 70 percent reduction in the median case.

I also added two new tests for gfx950 and k 2048, to make sure we're covering the different numbers of splits and graph capture and replay.

I've checked this with a CPU model on all 35 shapes mentioned in the issue, and the result is an exact match with exact top-k for all of them. The kernel compiles fine for gfx950, and I'll provide timings on MI355X in this PR.
